title: Initialize the canonical match from approved lobby configuration
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/SWARM_PILOT.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md and the frozen sources under docs/design/ first. RULES-SPEC-v1.md is the canonical six-node deterministic gameplay contract; completed foundation APIs remain compatibility history. Implement new versioned APIs without changing the completed T01–T10 contracts. Work only in declared ownership; no manifests, shared exports or dependencies unless explicitly owned. Engine production remains ES2022-only, pure and independent from Firebase, Node, browser, UI and Capacitor. Use original synthetic test data and injected authority time/entropy; no clocks or global randomness in engine. Never expose seed, roles, private inputs or raw audit data through public output. Do not invent a rule where an explicit design gap is named. Run scoped lint/typecheck/tests and npm run check; report contract changes and observed results. No commits, pushes, PRs, child agents, cloud deployment, credentials or budget changes. Export createMatchV1 for5–10 fixed seats, existing temporary aliases/avatar references, host identity, injected private seed, catalog version and timer setting30/60/90/120 seconds. Compose merged roles/incident queue and create exact initial Repair0/Sabotage0/round/ShiftLead state without invoking Firebase or a UI prototype. Validate prerequisites atomically. Start eligibility is checked by the service, while pure initialization ensures a valid roster/configuration. Humans and bots occupy the same domain seats; the engine cannot privilege bots or expose other roles.
acceptance: Each supported size/timer creates reproducible state with the exact role table, valid first incident and intact private seed/RNG.
Malformed/full/undersized settings, unknown host/seat references and mismatched catalog versions fail before partial state is exposed.
Initialization uses actual canonical incident content and no hardcoded four-round demo, five-point victory or platform APIs.
Scoped lint, typecheck and tests plus npm run check pass; legacy APIs retain compatibility and only owned files change.
